findings.claim: Keyword-order and intervening-kwarg writable open/Path.open/io.open of a protected path are allowed at 6aec78b and were denied at c715b24. Positional path-then-mode and mode= immediately after the path still deny. Path-as-data and path-as-read allows are the intended false-positive fix, not this hole. Semantic correction: decide a write from the call's mode (positional or mode=) and bind the path from the file positional or file= keyword regardless of keyword order; keep ignoring a protected path used only as data or as a read. Do not add another literal keyword-order regex.

findings.claim: dispatch_args advances one token after env or python and then takes that token as the program, so python3 -u launch.py, python3 -- launch.py, env -i launch.py, python3 -B/-O/-E/-s launch.py, and env --ignore-environment launch.py are allowed at 6aec78b and were denied at c715b24. Bare launch.py, python3 launch.py, and env FOO=bar launch.py still deny; pgrep with launch.py as an argument correctly allows. Semantic correction: skip non-consuming interpreter and env options and -- until the operand; stop without treating a consuming option's argument (-c, -m, env -u NAME) as the program; refuse when that operand's command word is launch.py. Do not restore a first-three-tokens scan; that re-breaks pgrep.

findings.claim: SWEEP_CLIPPED matches only | head -N and | head -n N (space required), so GNU head -n5 and --lines=5 after an allowed tail are allowed at 6aec78b. The same composition was denied at c715b24 because CLIPPED matched the tail, not the head. Standalone head -n5 and --lines=5 were already allowed at the base. | tail alone is an intended allow (keep head, skip tail). | tail | head -5 and | head -n 5 still deny. Semantic correction: treat GNU head line-count operands (-N, -nN, -n N, --lines=N, --lines N) as one clip. Do not restore tail as a sweep clip.
